scope: Bounded independent review of 13 named-core models and corresponding chemistry.json note sections; no new broad source audit.

findings.detail: 1.60C prescribes an aqueous-solution electrolysis practical, not molten PbBr2. Remove 1.60C from this model; 1.58C supports the molten case.
The specific salt-solution displacement requirement is 2.16. Replace 2.15 with 2.16; 2.15 concerns water/dilute-acid reactivity observations. Other references may remain as contextual skills.
Explicitly state suitable inert electrodes in the model and matching note condition to retain the 1.58C experimental boundary. Products, polarity and stated hot phases are correct.

checked: All 13 overall equations conserve atoms; supplied formulas and practice corrections are consistent.
Molten lead is correctly liquid in the stated hot apparatus and solid after cooling; bromine is diatomic.
Concentrated brine specifies inert electrodes and separated products; dilute-solution competition is qualified.
CuSO4 electrolysis specifies inert electrodes and distinguishes an active copper anode; acidification equation balances.
Acidified-water sulfuric acid is electrolyte, not an overall consumed reactant; 2:1 gas volumes require matched conditions.
CuSO4 dehydration uses hot-region steam and controlled heating; hydration explicitly limits the pentahydrate stoichiometric model and distinguishes excess-water solution.
NH4Cl reversal distinguishes cool deposition from closed-system equilibrium and avoids a heated sealed vessel.
Marble/peroxide gas identities, neutralization and zinc displacement answers are chemically consistent.
Paper 2C electrolysis models are labelled; wholeCollectionComplete, humanReviewed and practicalTrialsPerformed remain false.
limits: Written chemistry/source-reference review only. No experimental trial, empirical calibration, whole-collection completion, rendered layout verification or template activation.
